chunks: From him, from one of his companions, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Fuzayl ibn Uman, from Rabi'a al-Ra'y who said:

I saw in the hand of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) an embedded stone of carnelian, so I said, 'What is this stone?' So he said: 'Roman carnelian'. And he said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who wears a ring with the carnelian, his needs would be fulfilled'.

key_terms.تَخَتَّمَ: To wear a ring (literally: to be like a camel with a ring in its nose)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of wearing a ring with carnelian according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practice of the Imams, specifically Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), wearing a ring with a Roman carnelian (*aqiq rumi*), linking material adornment to spiritual efficacy. It underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory and beneficial power of specific stones, rooted in the Prophet’s promise that such adornment facilitates the fulfillment of one's needs (*qadit hawa'ijuhu*). This reflects the broader tradition of *takhattum* (wearing rings) as a means of invoking divine assistance and maintaining a tangible connection to prophetic sunnah.

en.hubeali: From him, from one of his companions, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Fuzayl Bin usman, from Rabi’a Al Raiy who said,

‘I saw in the hand of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> an embedded stone of carnelian, so I said, ‘What is this stone?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Roman carnelian’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who wears a ring with the carnelian, his needs would be fulfilled’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from certain persons of his people from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from Fudayl ibn ‘Uthman from Rabi‘ah al-Ra’iy who has said the following:

“Once on the hand of abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, I saw carnelian as the stone of the ring, and asked, ‘What is this stone?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is a Roman carnelian. The Messenger of Allah has said, “If one uses carnelian as his ring his wishes come true.’””
